title: Consultancy & Agroforestry Advisors
excerpt: Build consistent, evidence-led agroforestry scenarios for client strategy, design and investment planning.
need: Advisors need a repeatable way to connect site conditions, species choices, management assumptions and financial expectations.
use: FarmTree can help teams compare options, document assumptions and turn modelling outputs into a clearer client decision process.
challenges: Keeping site, species and price assumptions consistent across assignments
Explaining long-term trade-offs without hiding uncertainty
Producing reviewable outputs efficiently
workflow: Define the client decision, assemble available site data, compare a small set of designs, review assumptions with specialists, and export the selected scenario for the advisory process.
faq: Does FarmTree replace specialist judgement?
No. It structures scenario evidence; professional and local judgement remain essential.

title: Development Banks & Donor Organisations
excerpt: Assess agroforestry programmes with clearer assumptions, comparable scenarios and long-term impact context.
need: Finance and donor teams need transparent project logic before committing resources and a consistent basis for later review.
use: FarmTree can structure scenario comparisons across economic, environmental and operational considerations without replacing due diligence.
challenges: Comparing programmes built on different assumptions
Reviewing long time horizons before funding decisions
Connecting planning evidence to later monitoring
workflow: Agree on the appraisal question, model representative project scenarios, document sensitivity and data gaps, then use the outputs alongside technical, financial and safeguards due diligence.
faq: Are projections investment assurance?
No. They are decision-support evidence and do not replace due diligence or independent assurance.

title: NGOs & Conservation Organisations
excerpt: Connect conservation goals and livelihood priorities to practical agroforestry planning and monitoring.
need: Programme teams often need to balance ecological objectives, farmers’ circumstances and implementation constraints across varied sites.
use: FarmTree can make assumptions and trade-offs visible so programmes can compare designs and communicate their planning rationale.
challenges: Balancing livelihood and conservation priorities
Adapting programme designs across sites
Separating measured progress from modelled futures
capabilities: Production, carbon, water and economic indicators
workflow: Frame the programme outcomes with field teams, model locally relevant options, select indicators for validation, and retain a clear record of assumptions.
faq: Can local teams update scenarios?
Yes, subject to training, data access and the agreed project workflow.

title: NbS & Carbon Project Developers
excerpt: Test agroforestry design choices and connect project assumptions to carbon, production and financial scenarios.
need: Nature-based solution developers need coherent project assumptions that can be examined before monitoring and verification workflows begin.
use: FarmTree can support early scenario design and planning evidence; independent standards, validation and verification remain separate.
challenges: Testing design feasibility before validation
Connecting carbon assumptions to farmer and project value
Maintaining clear boundaries between projection and verification
workflow: Use FarmTree during design to compare systems and sensitivities, then pass clearly labelled inputs and projections into the project's independent standards and verification process.
faq: Does FarmTree certify carbon credits?
No. Certification, validation and verification are independent processes.

title: MRV & ESG Platforms
excerpt: Add forward-looking agroforestry scenario context to monitoring, reporting and sustainability workflows.
need: Reporting platforms need traceable assumptions and meaningful context around the field and project data they organise.
use: FarmTree can provide modelling outputs and scenario logic for integration planning, subject to an agreed technical scope and data contract.
challenges: Adding forward-looking context to observed datasets
Keeping provenance clear across systems
Representing agroforestry-specific assumptions
capabilities: Integration scoping for approved data exchanges
workflow: Map the reporting question and data contract, validate a limited integration use case, document modelled and measured fields, then review governance before scaling.
faq: Is a public API available?
Integration options are scoped with FarmTree; no public integration should be assumed without an agreement.

title: Government & Parastatal Institutions
excerpt: Compare agroforestry programme options using consistent site, species, management and impact assumptions.
need: Public institutions need transparent planning methods that can support programme design across regions and stakeholder groups.
use: FarmTree can help technical teams explore scenarios and communicate trade-offs while policy and procurement decisions remain with the institution.
challenges: Comparing regional programme options consistently
Communicating assumptions across technical and policy teams
Working within procurement and data-governance requirements
workflow: Select representative locations, agree policy-relevant questions, compare scenarios with technical teams, and use the evidence within established governance and procurement processes.
faq: Does FarmTree make policy decisions?
No. It supports technical analysis; accountable institutions retain policy and procurement decisions.

title: Industry Associations & Multi-Stakeholder Platforms
excerpt: Create a shared scenario language for agroforestry discussions across members, value chains and landscapes.
need: Multi-stakeholder initiatives need a consistent way to compare assumptions without obscuring differences between locations or participants.
use: FarmTree can support structured workshops and scenario conversations with a common evidence base for planning.
challenges: Creating shared definitions across members
Comparing options without erasing local differences
Turning discussion into reviewable next steps
workflow: Agree on a shared question, prepare representative scenarios, review trade-offs in a facilitated session, and record where local validation or member-specific analysis is needed.
faq: Can one scenario represent every member?
Usually not. Representative scenarios support discussion but should not replace local analysis.

title: Large Agri-Corporate
excerpt: Explore agroforestry options across sourcing landscapes with clearer business, production and environmental assumptions.
need: Agricultural companies need to understand how design choices may affect farmer value, production, resilience and programme planning over time.
use: FarmTree can compare representative scenarios and help teams define questions for field validation and investment review.
challenges: Connecting landscape goals to farmer value
Comparing programme designs across sourcing regions
Avoiding unsupported claims in sustainability reporting
workflow: Start with a named programme and decision, model representative systems, validate assumptions with local teams, and use results alongside supply-chain and field evidence.
faq: Are modelled results corporate reporting evidence?
They must be clearly labelled as projections and combined with appropriate measured evidence.

title: Social Enterprise
excerpt: Connect an agroforestry mission to practical operating assumptions, farmer value and an investable planning narrative.
need: Social enterprises need to test how ecological aims, operating choices and financial expectations fit together as they grow.
use: FarmTree can help teams compare models, clarify assumptions and prepare a stronger basis for partner or investor conversations.
challenges: Testing mission and operating assumptions together
Working with limited technical capacity
Explaining value and uncertainty to partners
workflow: Define the operating model, test a focused set of scenarios, identify the assumptions that matter most, and use the results to plan validation and partner conversations.
faq: Is FarmTree suitable for an early-stage organisation?
It can be when there is a clear decision, sufficient input data and an appropriately scoped engagement.

title: Investors
excerpt: Review agroforestry opportunities through transparent scenarios, assumptions and long-term value drivers.
need: Investors need a clear view of the biological, operational and financial assumptions behind an agroforestry proposition.
use: FarmTree can support scenario review and sensitivity discussions; it does not provide investment advice, assurance or a guarantee of outcomes.
challenges: Understanding biological and financial assumptions together
Testing sensitivity across long time horizons
Distinguishing projections from verified performance
capabilities: Traceable production, carbon and financial assumptions
workflow: Review the project's source data and model assumptions, compare downside and alternative scenarios, identify diligence questions, and combine the evidence with independent technical and financial review.
faq: Does FarmTree provide investment advice?
No. FarmTree provides modelling and decision-support information, not regulated investment advice or a guarantee.
